findings.title: Sender check crashes for integrations without sender metadata
findings.body: integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] assumes every pre-existing Integration has metadata['sender'] as a dict with 'login'. Integrations created through the normal pipeline do not guarantee this: build_integration only sets metadata['sender'] when state.get('sender') is present, and no pipeline view binds 'sender', so pipeline-created integrations lack it. If such an integration later exists without an OrganizationIntegration (e.g. removed from one org and reinstalled on another), this line raises KeyError/TypeError and returns a 500 instead of the friendly installation-failed page or a successful reinstall.

findings.title: Authenticated-user check is bypassed when Integration row does not yet exist
findings.body: When Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() without comparing pipeline state 'github_authenticated_user' to the installer. The sender check at lines 500-505 therefore only runs if the installation webhook has already created the Integration row. An attacker who knows/guesses a predictable GitHub installation_id and starts the claim flow before the webhook is processed (or where the webhook never creates the row) can complete installation as any authenticated GitHub user, defeating the validation this PR is meant to add; build_integration fetches only account info, not the installing user, so no later check compensates.

findings.title: Token exchange and user-info calls can raise unhandled exceptions
findings.body: safe_urlopen at line 423 is outside the try/except (which only covers safe_urlread/parse at lines 425-429), and get_user_info(payload['access_token']) at line 434 is also unguarded. A network error, TLS error, or non-2xx/invalid response from GitHub's /user endpoint will propagate as an unhandled 500 instead of rendering the intended 'Invalid installation request' error page described in the PR for bad/reused codes and verification failures.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 path
findings.body: The rewritten test first requests setup with only installation_id, which now just redirects into the new OAuthLoginView, and then requests setup with a deliberately wrong state value, so it fails at the state-signature check in OAuthLoginView before build_integration/get_installation_info is ever reached. The assertion for 'Invalid installation request.' therefore passes even if the GitHub 404 handling in build_integration is broken, leaving that behavior untested under the new flow.
